#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=100c100
#   --output=/home-mscluster/npather/disentangle/100c100.%A_%a.txt
#   --partition=stampede
#   --array=0-2

#flux: --job-name=100c100
#flux: -n 1

# Omitted Slurm option: --array=0-2
# Flux job arrays are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
# Performance implication: you must submit multiple jobs manually, increasing scheduler overhead and potentially reducing throughput.

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=stampede
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on different hardware or have different priority/limits (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --output=... with %A/%a tokens
# Slurm tokens %A (job id) and %a (array index) are not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

python3 main.py \
  --aicrowd_challenge=false \
  --name=100c100 \
  --alg=BetaVAE \
  --traverse_z=true \
  --traverse_c=true \
  --dset_dir=/home-mscluster/npather/disentanglement-pytorch/data/dsprites \
  --dset_name=dsprites_full \
  --encoder=PadlessGaussianConv64 \
  --decoder=SimpleConv64 \
  --discriminator=SimpleDiscriminator \
  --z_dim=20 \
  --use_wandb=true \
  --w_kld=1.0 \
  --w_tc=9.0 \
  --lr_G=0.001 \
  --lr_scheduler=ReduceLROnPlateau \
  --lr_scheduler_args mode=min factor=0.95 patience=1 min_lr=0.00005 \
  --max_iter=90000 \
  --iterations_c=90000 \
  --max_c=100 \
  --evaluat \
  --evaluation_metric mig sap_score irs dci beta_vae_sklearn factor_vae_metric \
  --alg=BetaVAE \
  --loss_terms \
  --use_bandit=false \
  --controlled_capacity_increase=true \
  --loss_txt=false \
  --wandb_project_name=anneal \
  --qma_alpha=0.001 \
  --boltzmann_lambda=15

reasons: The original Slurm job used an array (`--array=0-2`) but the Flux resource section has no array/loop mechanism; this changes the intended number of task instances to be run.

The original Slurm job targeted a specific partition (`--partition=stampede`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition constraint; this can change the allocated hardware and scheduling behavior.
issues: The command line contains `--evaluat` which looks like a truncated/invalid flag; this may cause the application to fail.
The argument `--alg=BetaVAE` appears twice; may be redundant or unintended.
